title: Dissection of mouse EDL and Soleus muscles
author: Anita Broellochs
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.pp9dmr6

steps.title: Pin leg and add Ringer
steps.instruction: Pin the mouse leg in a flexed position to a dissecting dish and immediately cover it with Ringer solution.

steps.title: Remove skin and fascia (Soleus)
steps.instruction: For Soleus extraction, remove the skin of the leg and carefully excise all surrounding fascia.

steps.title: Open gap and cut Achilles tendon
steps.instruction: Hold the Achilles tendon with forceps, use the bodkin side of the scissors to rub a gap between the Achilles tendon and the adjacent tendons, and when the gap appears, cut the Achilles tendon as close as possible to the foot.

steps.title: Enlarge gap and cut proximal tendon
steps.instruction: Allow the gap to open naturally toward the knee; if fascia still holds it, cut the fascia, then cut the tendon as close as possible to the knee, exposing the darker‑pink Soleus muscle.

steps.title: Release Soleus and cut lower tendon
steps.instruction: Grasp the upper tendon of the Soleus with forceps, pull the muscle slowly while cutting any remaining fascia, then cut the lower tendon (cutting the Achilles tendon is acceptable and can be cleaned afterwards).

steps.title: Clean and store Soleus muscle
steps.instruction: Separate the Soleus from the leg, remove all leftover fascia, transfer it to a new dissecting dish, pin it as shown, cover with Ringer solution, and store at 4 °C.

steps.title: Pin leg stretched for EDL
steps.instruction: Pin the mouse leg into a stretched position in a dissecting dish.

steps.title: Remove fascia for EDL
steps.instruction: Remove all fascia from the leg to expose the lower‑leg tendons.

steps.title: Identify and cut distal EDL tendons
steps.instruction: Locate the four EDL tendon ends next to the V‑shaped tibialis tendon, lift them with forceps (toes should stretch), and cut each tendon as close as possible to the foot.

steps.title: Open pocket and free EDL muscle
steps.instruction: After cutting the distal tendons, a pocket opens; remove any remaining fascia, free the EDL muscle from the pocket until the upper tendon is visible.

steps.title: Cut upper EDL tendon
steps.instruction: Cut the upper tendon of the EDL muscle.

steps.title: Clean and store EDL muscle
steps.instruction: Separate the EDL from the leg, removing all fascia and fat.

steps.title: Transfer muscles to PFA
steps.instruction: Move both dissected muscles to a clean dissecting dish, pin them lightly stretched, and cover with 3.7% paraformaldehyde (PFA).

steps.title: Seal and store overnight
steps.instruction: Cover the dish with parafilm and store at 4 °C overnight.
